extracted.intended_audience: examination staff at the German Patent and Trade Mark Office; patent applicants and their representatives (patent attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on substantive and procedural examination of patent applications at the DPMA, including claim content rules, priority claims, communications, hearings, time limits, amendments, and decision drafting. Aimed at ensuring consistent examiner practice and informing applicants of procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing process claim content
rubrics_metrics.description: For manufacturing processes, the patent claim must contain the indication of the original material and the chronological sequence of action applied to the original material / final product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional features of an apparatus capable of explaining the steps of the process are allowable. Distinguish manufacturing processes (aim to modify final product) from working processes (do not aim to modify final product, e.g., measuring, conveying). Use claims are classified under process claims and are directed at protection of the use of a mostly known matter for achieving a certain effect or final product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority claim requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority of earlier German applications for the same invention may be claimed provided the patent application was filed within twelve months from the date of filing of the earlier application and provided a domestic or foreign priority has not already been claimed for the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration of priority must be made together with the indication of the file number of the earlier application within two months from the filing date of the later application (section 40 (4) Patent Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Second subsequent application priority (new features)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to claim priority for a second subsequent application based on a subsequent application for such features not contained in the first application, but disclosed only in the first subsequent application, provided the inventions are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 4 F of the Paris Convention applies; a new priority right for newly introduced features is created by the second subsequent application. In that case, the first subsequent application as well as the original application are deemed withdrawn (section 40 (5) Patent Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed withdrawal when earlier application pending
rubrics_metrics.description: If the earlier application whose priority is claimed is still pending before the DPMA, it is deemed withdrawn as soon as the declaration of priority is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international (PCT) applications designating/electing Germany, deemed withdrawal may occur only after expiry of the 31-month time limit unless an explicit request for earlier examination/processing was filed. The examining section may at its discretion process the earlier application or wait until deemed withdrawal becomes effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign (Convention) priority requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority of an earlier foreign application may be claimed if the earlier application was effectively filed in a contracting party of the Paris Convention or under another international treaty; priority in a non-treaty state may be claimed under reciprocity conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where foreign priority is claimed, particulars (date, country, file number and a copy of the earlier application) must be furnished before expiry of the 16th month following the priority date (section 41 (1) Patent Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of validity of priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid claim to priority is to be examined only if documents dating from the priority interval and relevant for the decision were found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No interim decision is taken as to the valid claim to priority; if the priority claim is not effective, a decision on the application as a whole must be taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-invention test for priority and incompatibility of mixed priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter of a patent application concerns the same invention as the earlier application if the claimed combination of features is disclosed to the skilled person in the earlier application in its totality as belonging to the invention applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual features with different priority cannot be combined in one and the same patent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and drawings check
rubrics_metrics.description: If the abstract has not yet been published, the examiner must check whether the abstract pursuant to section 36 has been filed and does not have obvious deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where several drawings are mentioned in the concise summary and it is not clear which drawing most clearly characterises the invention, the examining section determines which drawing characterises the invention (section 36 (2) sentence 3). See also naming of inventor (section 37).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and style of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications in the examination procedure serve to prepare the grant or the refusal of the patent and must be drafted in a clear and neutral style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of communications is determined by the obligation to inquire into the facts, to grant the right to be heard and by particular circumstances in the individual case. The applicant should be invited to revise the description only after patentable claims have been submitted or proposed by the examining section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications must propose positive claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A communication should not only state those aspects which are an obstacle to grant, but also provide positive proposals for amending the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should clearly show the applicant whether and to what extent the examining section considers the subject matter of the application to be patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing applicant when no patentable subject matter is identifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examining section cannot identify any patentable subject matter in the application documents, it is to inform the applicant accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The communication should specify, in particular, that no grantable main claim can be proposed and that the application is likely to be refused even if new claims should be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and reasoning in discussing prior art and inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications must be understandable; publications on the state of the art must not be discussed by sweeping references to their overall content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of a comparison of features, the examining section has to explain, with reference to text passages and figures, why a subject matter in the state of the art conflicts with the subject matter of the application. If not based on an inventive step, the communication must state why the skilled person had a motivation to combine publications or expert knowledge, and provide conclusive reasoning on inventive step including the motivation of the person skilled in the art to avoid retrospective view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unambiguity and structure of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication must contain unambiguous statements or requests allowing the applicant to get a clear picture of the opinion of the examining section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a communication deals with several individual problems (formal deficiencies or patentability), it should be subdivided into numbered sections. Facts relevant to the decision must be handled preferentially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation management in communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications cited for the first time in a communication should be listed at the beginning and provided with consecutive numbers maintained throughout the procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serial numbers of new citations introduced in later communications should be added at the end of the list established earlier. For readability it may be useful to fully quote citations at the beginning and indicate their serial numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content of the first communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The first communication – provided it concerns a first filing and the applicant has requested examination in good time – should be issued early enough to be sent to the applicant four months before expiry of the priority year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A search and an opinion on the patentability of all claimed subject-matter is necessary. A detailed opinion on subsidiary claims is indispensable. At the beginning of the first communication, the skilled person must be defined. If necessary, the examiner must interpret the subject matter or make assumptions for the examination and inform the applicant. Lack of unity should be raised in the first communication if found. An outline of independent claim features can be made at the beginning after mentioning relevant publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second and subsequent communications policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The second communication about substantive examination, if required, should in general be the last one and lead to a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To streamline procedure, a hearing should, as far as possible, take precedence over further communications. An opinion once carefully reached should only be revised if the applicant submits equally substantiated and convincing counter-arguments or if new facts/legal situation arise; reasons must be given for any revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting and granting time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The DPMA aims to complete the examination within a reasonable period if requested by the applicant; the applicant should reply to communications within fixed time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining section should estimate time required and fix appropriate limits. A one-month time limit usually sufficient for formal deficiencies; four months normally for substantive communications. Consider examiner workload. For an application whose priority is claimed in a pending European application designating Germany, up to twelve months may be granted (even repeatedly). If communication not answered, immediate decision may be taken. First request for extension usually granted even if grounds briefly stated; further extensions granted if sufficiently reasoned. Requests for extension must be rejected by a separate decision and may be combined with decision on subject matter. Implicit one-month extension may be granted for procedural economy in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings: authority and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The examining section may at any time summon and hear the parties, examine witnesses and experts, and institute other inquiries necessary to clarify the matter. The examiner chairs hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may attend only with applicant's consent. The applicant must be heard on request. Hearings can be convenient for conducting the procedure speedily and can conclude the procedure by delivery of decision at the hearing. Hearings and demonstrations are useful where ambiguity exists or patentability questions cannot be clarified in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and conduct of hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: In preparation for hearings, the examining section and the applicant must be familiar with the matter and case file; issues not previously considered should be indicated in the summons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hearing took place before a change of examining section, repeat only if new section has serious reasons. At the beginning of hearing the applicant/representative must identify himself. A non-lawyer representative must produce power of attorney. The examining section should first outline controversial issues and may submit proposals. If agreement reached on patentability, wording of claims and structure of description should be laid down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing minutes requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Minutes must reproduce the essentials of the hearing and include place, date, persons attending and course of the hearing; new state of the art or legal aspects introduced; and all legally relevant declarations altering subject matter or affecting procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examining section deviates from previous opinion, minutes must show reasons. Minutes must be signed by the examining section and parties receive a copy. Parties are advised to countersign legally relevant declarations (not a prerequisite). Provisional shorthand or tape recording admissible but a written version must be produced without delay and the minutes must mention the provisional recording and its approval or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of decisions at hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, a decision of the examining section should be pronounced at the end of the hearing; the delivery and operative part must be included in the minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The representative's request for consultation is not sufficient to postpone decision. When delivering the decision, announcing the operative part and referring to the written reasons is sufficient; the written statement of reasons must be prepared without delay. The DPMA is bound by the delivered decision; submissions received after delivery may not be taken into consideration except on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uninvited calls and telephone communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls to the examining section without invitation should be briefly noted in the files; immediate hearing is discretionary. Telephone conversations can further completion of examination but cannot replace written communications that notify substantive comments of considerable importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone conversations are useful to briefly discuss wording, clarify doubts regarding new documents, request fair copies, etc. The examiner in charge or higher official is to make a note in the case file on the telephone conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote participation in hearings/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in hearings and takings of evidence using image and sound transmission is permitted under section 128a of the Code of Civil Procedure (applied correspondingly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examining section may permit parties to stay at another location and perform procedural acts from there; image and sound are broadcast in real time. The decision on this is incontestable (section 46(1) sentence 2 in conjunction with section 128a (3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and inadmissible extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must not contain inadmissible extensions (see section 38 of the Patent Act). Requests for amendments must be limited to the necessary extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file fair copies incorporating changes to claims or description (section 15 (1) sentence 2 Patent Ordinance). If amendments were not proposed by the DPMA, the applicant must indicate in which part of the original documents each inventive feature described in the new documents is disclosed (section 15 (3) Patent Ordinance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing of patent documents and language considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent specifications are official publications and must not contain indications whose publication would be contrary to ordre public or morality. The applicant is responsible for accurately worded specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examining section need not edit documents if they are clearly drafted and acceptable; respect the particularities of the applicant's language since revisions could amount to inadmissible amendments. If an applicant agrees by telephone to a modification, the modification must be confirmed in writing. Documents can no longer be modified after delivery of the decision to grant except in case of review after appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions of the examining section: form and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Any DPMA statement resulting in a final regulation that may affect rights constitutes a decision. Decisions must be well-founded and a copy must be served ex officio to parties concerned (section 47 (1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should contain a caption (parties), an operative part (tenor), and a statement of reasons consisting of facts of the case and reasons for the decision. Facts should briefly describe essential claims and means of attack/defence; reasons must cover all points relevant to the decision and state in detail all considerations on which the decision is based. Quotation of unpublished decisions should be avoided if possible, though the examining section may adopt views and reasons from unpublished decisions.
